output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Deploying a frozen single-sample classifier}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Fit the reference scorer on training data, save it, and score a new specimen.
The example uses simulated abundances and needs only OmicSelector's core R
Imports. Rendering this document also needs knitr and rmarkdown.

```{r reference}
library(OmicSelector)
set.seed(2610)
X <- matrix(rexp(41 * 30), 41, 30,
            dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("marker", 1:30)))
y <- rep(0:1, each = 20)
X[21:40, 1:5] <- X[21:40, 1:5] * 3
X_train <- X[1:40, , drop = FALSE]
x_new <- X[41, , drop = FALSE]
frozen <- deploy_singlesample(X_train, y, method = "ws-rclr-trimmed")
model_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(frozen, model_file)
frozen <- readRDS(model_file)
score_specimen(frozen, x_new, strict = TRUE)
stopifnot(is_singlesample_deployable(frozen, X_train[1:8, , drop = FALSE]))
unlink(model_file)
```

The score is a signed panel score, not a calibrated disease probability.
Training fixes the features and weights. Scoring uses the incoming specimen
and that frozen state. Keep the feature names, measurement units, assay
conversion and non-detect policy consistent with training. Use the existing
frozen preprocessor for counts or Ct measurements when needed.

The audit checks that a specimen's score does not depend on companion specimens
and that scoring leaves the model unchanged. It does not establish clinical
performance or a diagnostic threshold.

```{r requirements}
method_requirements("ws-rclr-trimmed")
available_methods("ws-rclr-trimmed", python = FALSE)
install_method_dependencies(c("ai-tabpfn", "tab-tabicl"), dry_run = TRUE)
```

Use `method_requirements()` to compare required software and recorded PB1 costs.
The `measurements` attribute retains the individual datasets, measuring node,
CPU, device and settings. Missing timings mean unmeasured or unsuccessful;
they do not mean zero cost. Runtime also depends on panel and training-set size.

To add a method, run its printed `install_command`. Run the Python installer
in a fresh R session. In later sessions set `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to the virtual
environment's interpreter before loading OmicSelector. Python-trained methods
that export plain R parameters can retain their existing R scoring routes.
Foundation models need their recorded Python backend and weights at deployment.

The benchmark found no method with a statistically significant improvement over
the reference under the prespecified comparison. This does not establish equal
performance between methods. Choose a method that fits the assay, available
metadata and deployment resources, then validate its performance for the
intended setting. The release's `paper/` reproduction folder records the
analysis and source tables when the completed R16 bundle is included.
